75.s: He replaced Charlie Miller, drafted, in Barnet's band with Peanuts Holland and Howard McGhee; Andy Gibson arranged.
75.ch: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
75.q: Yeah? I didn't know that. Well, I remember Charlie when he used to come up to... He was a great admirer of Benny Carter. He used to go into the Empire Ballroom, I remember. Well, now, he was stuck for a piano player at the point, and that's the way I came in, you know. It was mostly road...

75.t: Charlie Barnet as a boss; leaving and joining Kirby
75.s: Barnet was great but often absent; he advised Ramirez not to be broke; Ralph Burns replaced Ramirez and he later joined John Kirby.
75.ch: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
75.q: He was great. Charlie was beautiful. He was a fine fellow. But he didn't stay with the band much. I think Charlie had other problems, I guess, bringing a vocalist here, a vocalist there...

13.t: How the 1931 Hines band differed from the first
13.s: Hines wanted a bigger band; Ed Fox knew nothing about music.
13.q: No, it was Earl. Wasn't Ed Fox, because he didn't know nothing about music.

13.t: The 1936-37 personnel turnover in the Hines band
13.s: Many sidemen quit or got notice; Ray Nance's men arrived.
13.q: Yeah, I was going to say '36, but I know -- that's when Hayes Alvis came into the band. We changed the brass section, they changed the -- little-George Dixon was still with us. Then we got Milton Fletcher on trumpet.

201.s: After the service he auditioned at Nola Studios, got the jazz chair, and then left for Woody Herman over the strictly written music.
201.ch: On the road with Spivak and Sauter-Finegan
201.q: Well that certainly was a huge learning experience for me. I had just come out of the service and I auditioned in the same studio, Nola Studios, not the Nola Studios that exists now in New York, but it was a rehearsal studio, a famous rehearsal studio on Broadway around 52nd Street I think it was.…

436.t: Teddy Powell, Woody Herman's call, Sonny Dunham and joining Will Bradley
436.s: Pete leaves Teddy Powell's band for the Herd, and recounts joining Dunham and Bradley, pay figures, Barnet, and Freddy Slack.
436.q: Well I was with the band — Teddy Powell had a band. And it was very similar as the First Herd in style. On that band was Buddy DeFranco on clarinet, and there was Boots Mussulli, and Charlie Ventura was on the band, and different guys, George Handy was writing charts for the band, and Eddie Finkel,…

668.t: Quitting and rejoining Flanagan, then Jack Teagarden at the Meadowbrook
668.s: After the tour he quit, rejoined Flanagan a year later, and auditioned for Teagarden while Flanagan complained about his own band.
668.q: I expected much more. From then on I just got very — like I said when I came home I said — oh boy they all said, you know, starry eyed, and thought I’d be stage struck. “How was it?” “It was the fucking worst” I said. Plain and simple. It was the fucking worst. Ohhhh. They all wanted to do that.…

206.t: Leaving Norvo for Claude Thornhill and the Schribman office
206.s: He and Gozzo left Norvo for Thornhill at Glen Island with Schribman backing; swing bands compared to rock bands.
206.q: I loved parts of it. And when I first left home with the Dick Stabile scene, I was so homesick, but then I outgrew it. You know you’d get to be buddies with the guys you worked with, and they’re like a family. I roomed with Conrad for two and a half years. We left Red Norvo’s band to go with Claude…

157.t: Woody's band breaks up; Covington's Dorsey band, Buddy Morrow and drummers
157.s: Hal left Woody, played with Warren Covington's Tommy Dorsey band, returned to split lead with Bill Chase, then joined Buddy Morrow at $175.
157.q: time, playing music that at the time I said if this is all I did the rest of my life — play this music — that’s all I’d ever want to do because the music was so much fun. I never played lead although the first time I was on Woody’s band I was playing like I said on one of the ends, Don was on the…

421.t: Leaving Miller, the partnership offer, and Tex Beneke replacing him
421.s: Miller broke up his first band; when he reorganized and offered a partnership, Jerry, already with Red Norvo, declined and rehearsed the saxes, where Tex Beneke took his place.
421.q: Well that’s a relative word, Monk, “tough.” Because they weren’t tough as far as I’m concerned. I understood Glenn. I was a confidante of Glenn’s. Glenn and I were close. I might tell you this it’s an interesting bit of history from my point of view, and that is I stayed with Glenn until he broke…

333.s: Leaving Don Redman at the Zanzibar, he joined Hawkins, whom he knew from Pensacola, and stayed twelve years in an unintegrated band.
333.q: Oh, how I joined Erskine’s? Well it’s easy. Erskine’s band stayed with us when we had our hotel, or whatever you called it—

351.t: Teddy Powell's band, Charlie Ventura and Marty's brother Teddy
351.s: Marty recounts Teddy Powell's band, Ventura leaving for Krupa, recommending his brother, and quitting Powell.
351.q: Grove Dictionary, right okay. Anyway so the Charlie Barnet thing was like I was sitting at home, I had just left Teddy Powell’s band or Lee Castle’s band. Teddy Powell’s band I think. That’s another story, that Teddy Powell was weird. Because in Teddy Powell’s band, we had Charlie Ventura on the…

416.t: Joining Woody Herman through Ralph Burns
416.s: Ralph Burns recommended him to Woody Herman and he left Russ Morgan's band; the nickname Flip came long before.
416.q: The first time with Woody Herman. I was with Russ Morgan before that. No I was with Red Norvo. And Ralph Burns was the piano player, and I went with Russ Morgan and Ralph went with Charlie Barnet and then he went with Woody, and Ralph told Woody about me. You know and I didn’t want to leave Russ…

28.t: Charlie Turner's band, a quarrel with his best friend, and Willy Bryant
28.s: His childhood German helped him get by; he left Charlie Turner's band by urgent request after a falling-out and then joined Willy Bryant's happy band.
28.ch: Berlin and the Turner and Bryant bands
28.q: So I got by. Of course, it took me some time to get myself straight because I was (inaudible). So what happened was that -- Charlie Turner's band, I stayed with Charlie Turner's band. And then I stayed up there quite some time. And then I had a little difficulty with my best friend in the band and…

234.t: Skinny Ennis takes over Gil's band
234.s: Gil describes how MCA put Ennis in front of his band, how its library changed to Ennis's sound and why he left.
234.ch: First bands, Ennis, Thornhill and the Army
234.q: When we first started I had, it was my band and my library you know. So he took the band over and the first couple of jobs we played he would stand out front and listen to it you know. And he liked it very much and when the number would be over he would applaud and everything, forgetting that he…

388.t: Getting Chubby Jackson and Ralph Burns hired
388.s: Hinton sorts out dates; Leeman says he got Chubby Jackson into Barnet's band in 1940 and recommended Ralph Burns to Woody Herman.
388.ch: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
388.q: Well, I got Chubby Jackson his job in Barnet's band recently -- I always needed a bass player.
